title: Arakhin 21
description: Chapter 5 closes with the baraita of the rented house and Rabbi Meir, taking collateral for valuations and offerings, coercing a man “until he says: I want to” and Shmuel and Ulla on consent, and chapter 6, Shum HaYetomim, opens with the public proclamation of orphans’ and consecrated property.
topics: 🏠 A rented house consecrated, and rent paid to the Temple: Rabbi Meir’s “an entity not yet in the world”
📜 Collateral is taken for valuations, burnt offerings and peace offerings, but not for sin and guilt offerings
🔄 Rav Pappa’s exceptions: the nazirite’s sin offering and the leper’s burnt offering
✋ “He shall sacrifice it… of his volition”: coerced until he says “I want to”
⚖️ Shmuel and Ulla: when does an offering brought for someone else need his consent?
📄 Rav Sheshet: a declaration that cancels a coerced bill of divorce
📖 Hadran: chapter 5, HaOmer Mishkali, ends and chapter 6, Shum HaYetomim, begins
📣 Proclaiming orphans’ and consecrated property: thirty and sixty days, morning and evening

a1.he: הִקְדִּישׁוֹ הַדָּר בּוֹ — מַעֲלֶה שָׂכָר לַהֶקְדֵּשׁ. הִקְדִּישׁוֹ הַדָּר בּוֹ? הֵיכִי מָצֵי מַקְדֵּישׁ לֵהּ? ״אִישׁ כִּי יַקְדִּישׁ בֵּיתוֹ קֹדֶשׁ״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא, מָה בֵּיתוֹ בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ — אַף כֹּל בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ! הָכִי קָאָמַר: הִקְדִּישׁוֹ מַשְׂכִּיר — הַדָּר בּוֹ מַעֲלֶה שָׂכָר לַהֶקְדֵּשׁ.

a2.he: הִקְדִּישׁוֹ מַשְׂכִּיר, הֵיכִי דָּיַיר בֵּיהּ? בִּמְעִילָה קָאֵי! וְתוּ מַעֲלֶה שָׂכָר לַהֶקְדֵּשׁ? כֵּיוָן דִּמְעַל בֵּיהּ, נָפֵיק לֵיהּ שָׂכָר לְחוּלִּין!

a3.he: דְּאָמַר: ״לִכְשֶׁיָּבֹא שְׂכָרוֹ יִקְדַּשׁ״, וְהָא אֵין אָדָם מַקְדִּישׁ דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בָּא לָעוֹלָם!

a4.he: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא, דְּאָמַר: אָדָם מַקְדִּישׁ דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בָּא לָעוֹלָם. אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַב מָרִי בַּר חָמָא לְרַב חִסְדָּא: כְּמַאן? כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר, דְּאָמַר: אָדָם מַקְדִּישׁ דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בָּא לָעוֹלָם? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְאֶלָּא כְּמַאן?!

a5.he: מַתְנִי׳ חַיָּיבֵי עֲרָכִין — מְמַשְׁכְּנִין אוֹתָן, חַיָּיבֵי חַטָּאוֹת וַאֲשָׁמוֹת — אֵין מְמַשְׁכְּנִין אוֹתָן, חַיָּיבֵי עוֹלוֹת וּשְׁלָמִים — מְמַשְׁכְּנִין אוֹתָן.

a6.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין מִתְכַּפֵּר לוֹ עַד שֶׁיִּתְרַצֶּה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״לִרְצוֹנוֹ״, כּוֹפִין אוֹתוֹ עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר: ״רוֹצֶה אֲנִי״. וְכֵן אַתָּה אוֹמֵר בְּגִיטֵּי נָשִׁים, כּוֹפִין אוֹתוֹ עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר: ״רוֹצֶה אֲנִי״.

a7.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: פְּעָמִים שֶׁחַיָּיבֵי חַטָּאוֹת מְמַשְׁכְּנִין אוֹתָן, חַיָּיבֵי עוֹלוֹת אֵין מְמַשְׁכְּנִין אוֹתָן.

a8.he: חַיָּיבֵי חַטָּאוֹת מְמַשְׁכְּנִין אוֹתָן בְּחַטַּאת נָזִיר, דְּכֵיוָן דְּאָמַר מָר: ״אִם גִּילַּח עַל אֶחָד מִשְּׁלׇשְׁתָּן יָצָא, וְאִם נִזְרַק עָלָיו אֶחָד מִן הַדָּמִים הוּתַּר הַנָּזִיר לִשְׁתּוֹת יַיִן וְלִיטַמֵּא לְמֵתִים״ — פָּשַׁע בַּהּ וְלָא מַיְיתֵי.

a9.he: חַיָּיבֵי עוֹלוֹת — אֵין מְמַשְׁכְּנִין אוֹתָן בְּעוֹלַת יוֹלֶדֶת.

a10.he: מַאי נִיהוּ דְּאַקְדְּמַיהּ קְרָא, וְהָאָמַר רָבָא: לְמִקְרָאָהּ הִקְדִּימָהּ הַכָּתוּב!

a11.he: אֶלָּא בְּעוֹלַת מְצוֹרָע, דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁחַטָּאתוֹ וַאֲשָׁמוֹ עֹיכַבְתּוֹ, כָּךְ עוֹלָתוֹ עֹיכַבְתּוֹ.

a12.he: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין מִתְכַּפֵּר לוֹ עַד שֶׁיִּתְרַצֶּה, תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״יַקְרִיב אוֹתוֹ״ — מְלַמֵּד שֶׁכּוֹפִין אוֹתוֹ, יָכוֹל בְּעַל כׇּרְחוֹ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״לִרְצוֹנוֹ״, הָא כֵּיצַד? כּוֹפִין אוֹתוֹ עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר ״רוֹצֶה אֲנִי״.

a13.he: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: עוֹלָה צְרִיכָה דַּעַת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״לִרְצוֹנוֹ״. מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן? תְּנֵינָא: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין מִתְכַּפֵּר לוֹ עַד שֶׁיִּתְרַצֶּה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״לִרְצוֹנוֹ״!

a14.he: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּפָרֵישׁ לֵיהּ חַבְרֵיהּ. מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: כִּי בָּעֵינַן דַּעַת מִדִּידֵיהּ, אֲבָל מִדְּחַבְרֵיהּ לָא? קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן, זִימְנִין דְּלָא נִיחָא לֵיהּ דְּלִיכַּפַּר בְּמִידֵּי דְּלָא דִּידֵיהּ.

b1.he: לְדַעַת — יָצָא, שֶׁלֹּא לְדַעַת — לֹא יָצָא.

b2.he: ״עוֹלָתוֹ וּשְׁלָמָיו שֶׁל פְּלוֹנִי עָלַי״, בֵּין לְדַעַת בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא לְדַעַת — יָצָא.

b3.he: אָמַר לְךָ שְׁמוּאֵל: כִּי תַּנְיָא הָהִיא בִּשְׁעַת כַּפָּרָה, דְּאִירַצִּי בִּשְׁעַת הַפְרָשָׁה, כִּי קָאָמֵינָא אֲנָא בִּשְׁעַת הַפְרָשָׁה.

b4.he: וּפְלִיגָא דְּעוּלָּא, דְּאָמַר עוּלָּא: לֹא חִילְּקוּ בֵּין חַטָּאת לְעוֹלָה, אֶלָּא שֶׁחַטָּאת צְרִיכָה דַּעַת בִּשְׁעַת הַפְרָשָׁה, וְעוֹלָה אֵין צְרִיכָה דַּעַת בִּשְׁעַת הַפְרָשָׁה, אֲבָל בִּשְׁעַת כַּפָּרָה — אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי לְדַעַת — יָצָא, שֶׁלֹּא לְדַעַת — לֹא יָצָא.

b5.he: מֵיתִיבִי: חַטָּאתוֹ וַאֲשָׁמוֹ עוֹלָתוֹ וּשְׁלָמָיו שֶׁל פְּלוֹנִי עָלַי, לְדַעַת — יָצָא, שֶׁלֹּא לְדַעַת — לֹא יָצָא!

b6.he: שְׁמוּאֵל מוֹקֵי לַהּ בִּשְׁעַת הַפְרָשָׁה, עוּלָּא מוֹקֵי לַהּ בִּשְׁעַת כַּפָּרָה. אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: מַתְנְיָיתָא אַהֲדָדֵי לָא קַשְׁיָין, הָא בִּשְׁעַת כַּפָּרָה, הָא בִּשְׁעַת הַפְרָשָׁה.

b7.he: (וְאָמוֹרָאֵי) [לְאָמוֹרָאֵי] נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא: שְׁמוּאֵל מוֹקֵי קַמַּיְיתָא בִּשְׁעַת כַּפָּרָה, בָּתְרָיְיתָא בִּשְׁעַת הַפְרָשָׁה, עוּלָּא מוֹקֵי אִיפְּכָא. אָמוֹרָאֵי וַדַּאי פְּלִיגִי. פְּשִׁיטָא!

b8.he: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: מַאי ״בִּשְׁעַת הַפְרָשָׁה״ דְּקָאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל? אַף בִּשְׁעַת הַפְרָשָׁה, וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּהָךְ קַמַּיְיתָא תְּיוּבְתֵּיהּ, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

b9.he: וְכֵן בְּגִיטֵּי נָשִׁים כּוֹפִין וְכוּ׳. אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: הַאי מַאן דְּמָסַר מוֹדָעָא אַגִּיטָּא — מוֹדָעֵיהּ מוֹדָעָא. פְּשִׁיטָא?

b10.he: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּעַשְּׂאוּהּ וְאִירַצִּי, מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: בַּטּוֹלֵי בַּטְּלֵיהּ, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

b11.he: דְּאִם כֵּן, לִיתְנֵי: עַד שֶׁיִּתֵּן! מַאי עַד שֶׁיֹּאמַר? עַד דִּמְבַטֵּל לֵיהּ לְמוֹדָעֵיהּ.

b13.he: מַתְנִי׳ שׁוּם הַיְּתוֹמִים — שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם, וְשׁוּם הַהֶקְדֵּשׁ — שִׁשִּׁים יוֹם, וּמַכְרִיזִין בַּבֹּקֶר וּבָעֶרֶב.

b14.he: גְּמָ׳ מַאי שְׁנָא בַּבֹּקֶר וּבָעֶרֶב? אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: בִּשְׁעַת הוֹצָאַת פּוֹעֲלִים וּבִשְׁעַת הַכְנָסַת פּוֹעֲלִים. בִּשְׁעַת הוֹצָאַת פּוֹעֲלִים — דְּאִיכָּא דְּנִיחָא לְמִיזְבַּן, אֲמַר לְהוּ לְפוֹעֲלִים: אֵיזִילוּ סַיְּירוּ לַהּ נִיהֲלַי. בִּשְׁעַת הַכְנָסַת פּוֹעֲלִים — דְּנִידְּכַר דְּאָמַר לְהוּ: נֵיזִיל נִישַׁיְּילִינְהוּ.

b15.he: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי: שׁוּם הַיְּתוֹמִים שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם, וְשׁוּם הַהֶקְדֵּשׁ שִׁשִּׁים יוֹם, וּמַכְרִיזִין בַּבֹּקֶר וּבְעָרֵב, בִּשְׁעַת הוֹצָאַת פּוֹעֲלִים וּבִשְׁעַת הַכְנָסַת פּוֹעֲלִים.

b16.he: אוֹמֵר: שְׂדֵה פְלוֹנִי בְּסִימָנֶיהָ וּבִמְצָרֶיהָ, כָּךְ הִיא יָפָה, וְכָךְ הִיא שׁוּמָא, כׇּל הָרוֹצֶה לִיקַּח יָבֹא וְיִקַּח, עַל מְנָת לִיתֵּן לְאִשָּׁה בִּכְתוּבָּתָהּ, וּלְבַעַל חוֹב בְּחוֹבוֹ.

b17.he: לְמָה לִי לְמֵימַר ״עַל מְנָת לִיתֵּן לְאִשָּׁה כְּתוּבָּתָהּ וּלְבַעַל חוֹב חוֹבוֹ״? דְּאִיכָּא דְּנִיחָא לֵיהּ בְּבַעַל חוֹב, דְּמֵיקֵל בְּזוּזֵי, וְאִיכָּא דְּנִיחָא לֵיהּ בְּאִשָּׁה, דְּשָׁקְלָה עַל יָד עַל יָד.

messages.text: Continued from 20b: some teach Rav Yehuda’s “this follows Rabbi Meir” about a different baraita, of one who rents a house to another and it is afflicted with leprosy: once the priest dismantles it, the owner must provide the renter with another house. The baraita goes on:
If the one living in it, i.e., the renter, consecrates the house, he pays the rent to the Temple treasury.

notes.he: קס"ד שהדר בו הקדישו:
notes.en: If the one living in it consecrates it, etc.: for now we assume that the one living in it [the renter] consecrated it.

notes.he: משכיר לשוכר שאין יכול לומר לו הרי שלך לפניך שהרי נותץ]:
notes.en: He is obligated to provide him a house: the lessor to the renter, for he cannot say to him, “Here is yours before you,” since it has been demolished. [This explains the end of 20b.]

notes.he: השוכר:
notes.en: Consecrated it: the renter.

messages.text: If the one living in the house consecrates it? How can the renter consecrate it? The Merciful One states: “When a man shall sanctify his house to be sacred” (Leviticus 27:14), from which it is derived that just as one’s house is in his possession, so too, anything that one consecrates must be in his possession. If so, the renter cannot consecrate the house, as he is not its owner.
messages.quote: the one living in it, i.e., the renter, consecrates

verse.he: וְאִישׁ כִּי־יַקְדִּשׁ אֶת־בֵּיתוֹ קֹדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה וְהֶעֱרִיכוֹ הַכֹּהֵן בֵּין טוֹב וּבֵין רָע כַּאֲשֶׁר יַעֲרִיךְ אֹתוֹ הַכֹּהֵן כֵּן יָקוּם׃
verse.en: Regarding anyone who consecrates a house to GOD: The priest shall assess it. Whether high or low, as the priest assesses it, so it shall stand;

notes.dh: הכי קאמר הקדישו משכיר הדר בו מעלה שכר להקדש
notes.he: תימה דהכא משמע דמשכיר יכול להקדיש ביתו אחר שהשכירו אע"ג דמשתעבד לשוכר ובכתובות פ' אף ע"פ (כתובות דף נט: ושם) אמר הא לא דמיא אלא לאומר שדה זו שמשכנתי לך לכשאפדנה תקדוש דקדשה משמע דווקא משום דקאמר לכשאפדנה אבל לאלתר לא מצי מקדיש לה הכא נמי לא מצי מקדיש ליה ובפ' איזהו נשך (ב"מ עג: ושם) אמרינן רב מרי בר רחל משכן ליה ההוא עובד כוכבים ביתא אזל זבניה לרבא נטר שתא ושקל אגר ביתא אמטי ליה לרבא א"ל האי דלא אמטאי אגר ביתא עד האידנא משום דהוה משכנתא ולא הוה עובד כוכבים מסלק ליה השתא נישקיל [מר] אגר ביתא משמע דיכול הלוה למכור וא"כ אמאי אינו יכול להקדיש מיד ואור"י דכן הדין המותר יותר מכנגד מעותיו הוא יכול להקדיש ולמכור מיד והא דאמר התם לכשאפדנה דמשמע אבל השתא אינו יכול להקדיש היינו כשהוא רוצה להקדיש הכל וההיא דאיזהו נשך (שם) זבין לו המותר והכא יכול להקדיש המותר והא דאמר הדר בו מעלה שכר להקדש היינו משום דיש לו להקדש שותפות עמו ואין כל אחד יכול לברר חלקו ויש מחלקין בין משכיר ללוה דדוקא לוה שלא תחזור אליו עוד בלא פרעון מעות ההוא ודאי לא מצי להקדיש אבל משכיר שלאחר השלמת זמן השכירות תחזור לו בחנם יכול הוא להקדיש מיהו ההיא דאיזהו נשך לא מיתרצא בהכי מיהו תימה דאשכחן בעלמא הקדיש לוה וזבין לוה משמע דמצי מקדישו ומזבין מיהו ב"ח מוציאו מיד ההקדש ומיד הלוקח כשירצה לגבות חובו אם אין לו לגבות ממקום אחר מידי דהוה אעשה עבדו אפותיקי מכרו או הקדישו דב"ח מוציא הימנו מיהו כל זמן שלא גבאו הוא קדוש ומכור הכא משמע דמשכיר יכול להקדיש הכי נמי יכול לאסור על השוכר וכן הלכה הכא משמע דאין השוכר יכול להקדיש מדפריך הדר בו היכי מצי מקדיש ליה איש כי יקדיש את ביתו אמר רחמנא מה ביתו ברשותו אף כל ברשותו וקשה דבתוספתא תניא אם הקדישו שוכר מקודשת ויש לומר הכא נמי השוכר מצי מקדיש ליה כל זמן שהוא ברשותו וה"ה דמצי אסר ליה לכולי עלמא כל ימי שכירותו והא דפריך הכא היכי מצי מקדיש ליה (והאי) [אהאי] דקאמר מעלה שכר להקדש (הכא) פריך והכי [פריך] היכי מצי מקדיש לענין דמעלה שכר הא אינו ברשותו מיהו תימה דהכא משמע דמשכיר מצי מקדיש ליה ובתוספתא תניא דאינה מקודשת וזה לשון תוספתא השוכר שדה מחבירו ועמד השוכר והשכירה לאחר רשאי בעל הבית שיאמר לו אין לי חשבון עם כל אדם אלא עמך עמד בעל הבית ומכרה מחשבין עם בעל הבית עמד בעל הבית והקדישה אינה מקודשת עד שתחזור לרשותו וכל מה שנהנה ממנו הרי זה מקודשת עמד השוכר והקדישה הרי זה מקודשת עד שתצא מרשותו ומעלה שכר להקדש עד כאן לשון התוספתא וי"ל דהא דתניא בתוספתא דאין המשכיר יכול להקדיש היינו כשהקדים לו שכרו והכא מיירי בשלא הקדים שכרו וה"נ איתא בירושלמי דמקום שנהגו המשכיר בית לחבירו ועמד והקדיש הרי זו מקודשת אימתי בזמן שלא הקדים לו שכרו אבל הקדים לו שכרו הרי זה דבריו חנם:
notes.en: In brief: Tosafot ask why the owner who rented out his house may consecrate it here, though it is pledged to the renter. In Ketubot (59b) it is compared to one who says, “This field that I mortgaged to you, when I redeem it, let it be consecrated,” which implies he cannot consecrate it at once; yet in Bava Metzia (73b) Rav Mari bar Raḥel, holding a gentile’s mortgaged house, sold it to Rava, which implies the borrower may sell it. The Ri answers: what exceeds the value of the lender’s money the owner may consecrate or sell at once; “when I redeem it” speaks of consecrating all of it, in Bava Metzia he sold the excess, and here he consecrates the excess, so the renter pays rent to the Temple because the Temple is his partner and neither can separate his share. Some distinguish a lessor, to whom the house returns free when the lease ends, from a borrower, to whom it returns only on repayment, though that does not settle Bava Metzia; and elsewhere a borrower consecrates and sells, and the creditor takes it back from the Temple or the buyer if he has nowhere else to collect, as with a slave made a security, while until then it is sacred and sold. So the lessor can consecrate the house, and likewise forbid it to the renter, and that is the halakha. The Gemara’s question implies the renter cannot consecrate it, yet the Tosefta teaches that if the renter consecrated it, it is consecrated: the renter can consecrate it while it is in his possession, and forbid it to everyone for his term; the question here was only how he could consecrate it so as to pay rent to the Temple. Last, the Tosefta (which Tosafot quote: an owner who consecrated his rented-out field, it is not consecrated until it returns to his possession; a renter who consecrated it, it is consecrated until it leaves his possession, and he pays rent to the Temple) says the lessor cannot consecrate: it speaks where the rent was paid in advance, and our case where it was not, as the Yerushalmi says: a lessor who consecrated, it is consecrated when the rent was not paid in advance; if it was, his words are void. notes.he: שלא (נתנגע) ברשותו (שלו):
notes.en: The one living in it: [the house is] not in his possession.

messages.text: This is what the baraita is saying: If the one renting out the house consecrates it, the one living in it pays the rent to the Temple treasury.

If the one renting out the house consecrates it, how is it possible for the renter to live in it? Since the house is consecrated property he is standing liable for the prohibition of misuse of consecrated property by living there!

notes.he: ואע"פ שלא פגם מעל כדתנן [ר"פ הנהנה] (דף יח.) הנהנה מן ההקדש ש"פ אע"פ שלא פגם מעל ואע"ג דאין מועלין במחובר לקרקע כדאיתא במס' מעילה פרק הנהנה מן ההקדש (שם:) צ"ל הך סוגיא דהכא אתיא כרב דאמר תלשו ולבסוף חברו הוי תלוש כדאמר המשתחוה לבית אסרו ובפרק הנהנה (דף כ. ושם) נמי מייתי לה לההיא דרב דאמר התם וכיון דבני להו מיהא מעל:
notes.en: If he lives in it, he stands in misuse: and even though he did not diminish it, he has misused it, as we learned (Me’ila 18a, beginning of chapter HaNehene): one who derives benefit worth a peruta from consecrated property, even though he did not diminish it, has misused it. And although there is no misuse with what is attached to the ground, as stated in tractate Me’ila, chapter HaNehene (18b), one must say that this passage follows Rav, who says that what was detached and later attached is considered detached, as he said that one who bows down to a house has rendered it forbidden. And in chapter HaNehene (20a) too it cites that statement of Rav, saying there: and since he built them, he has in any case misused them.

messages.text: And furthermore, why must he pay the rent to the Temple treasury? Since he misused consecrated property the payment of the rent immediately leaves the state of consecration and becomes non-sacred.

notes.he: [נפיק ליה שכר לחולין] ונ"ל דל"ג שכר וה"ג כיון דמעל נפיק ליה לחולין - כלומר משנהנה בתשמיש הבית ומעל יצא הבית לחולין כדתנן (מעילה דף יט:) אין מועל אחר מועל במוקדשין אלא בבהמה וכלי שרת בלבד וקרן וחומש אית ליה לשלומי ולא שכר להקדש דכל מידי דהקדש מכי מעל ביה נפיק לחולין דאמרינן במסכת מעילה (דף יח.) אין מעילה בכל מקום אלא שינוי וכן הוא אומר וימעלו בני ישראל מעל ביי' ויעבדו את הבעלים והיינו שינוי שמוציאו מהקדש לחול:
notes.en: [“The rent leaves to non-sacred status”:] It seems to me that we do not read “the rent”; rather the text reads: “Since he misused it, it leaves to non-sacred status.” That is, once he benefited from the use of the house and misused it, the house left consecration for non-sacred status, as we learned (Me’ila 19b): there is no misuse after misuse with consecrated items except with an animal and service vessels alone. And he must pay the principal and the added fifth, not rent to the Temple, since anything of the Temple’s, once one has misused it, leaves for non-sacred status, as we say in tractate Me’ila (18a): misuse everywhere means nothing but change, and so it says: “And the children of Israel committed a trespass against the Lord … and served the Baalim”; that is change, which takes it out of consecration into non-sacred status. [Rashi’s reading drops the word “rent” that the Davidson English translates; Tosafot (a2.2) defends it.]

notes.dh: הכי גרסינן כיון דמעל נפיק ליה שכר לחולין
notes.he: וכן הוא ברוב ספרים וה"פ כיון דמעל כו' כלומר שכר הבית נפיק לחולין שהרי חבירו הקדיש (השכיר) את הבית והוא לא ידע ומעל כשדר בו ונפיק ליה השוכר בתורת מעילה אבל אין לפרש כיון שמעל נפיק הבית לחולין וכפרש"י וקאמר לו ר"מ אמר על ההיא דתניא בתוספתא דמעילה (פ"ב) בקע בקרדום של הקדש ובא חבירו ובקע בו ובא חבירו ובקע בו כולם מעלו ובשילהי פרק הנהנה (מעילה יט:) תנן אין מועל אחר מועל בקדשים אלא בבהמה וכלי שרת היינו דקדושת הגוף לא מתחלל ע"י מעילה כמו קדושת דמים וקרדום לאו היינו כלי שרת אלא קדושת דמים הוא ולא יחשב כלי שרת מטעם שמביא אחרים לידי קדושת הגוף הוא עצמו לא כל שכן שיבא לידי קדושת הגוף דמהאי טעמא חשבינן שאר כלי שרת קדושת הגוף:
notes.en: This is how we read: “Since he misused it, the rent leaves to non-sacred status,” and so it is in most books. The meaning is: since he misused, and so on; that is, the rent of the house leaves for non-sacred status, since his fellow [the owner] consecrated the house without his knowing, and he misused it by living in it, and the renter discharges [the rent] by way of [payment for] misuse. But one cannot explain “since he misused, the house leaves for non-sacred status,” as Rashi explained. [The next words are unclear in the printed text; they seem to say that] R. M. pointed to what is taught in the Tosefta of Me’ila (ch. 2): one split wood with a consecrated axe, and his fellow came and split with it, and another came and split with it; all of them misused. And at the end of chapter HaNehene (Me’ila 19b) we learned: there is no misuse after misuse with consecrated items except with an animal and service vessels; that is, inherent sanctity is not deconsecrated through misuse as monetary sanctity is. And an axe is not a service vessel but has monetary sanctity, and it should not be counted as a service vessel on the ground that it brings other things to inherent sanctity; all the more so it does not itself come to inherent sanctity, which is the reason we count other service vessels as having inherent sanctity.

notes.he: מה שנהנה ממנו:
notes.en: Since he misused: what he benefited from it.

notes.he: נפק ליה שכר לחולין דמשום הכי חייב קרבן:
notes.en: The rent leaves for non-sacred status: for that reason he is liable to bring an offering.

messages.text: The baraita is discussing a case where the one renting out the house says: When the payment of the rent will come to me, the money shall be consecrated.

notes.he: השכר והבית לא הקדיש:
notes.en: When its rent comes, it shall be consecrated: [he consecrated] the rent, and the house he did not consecrate.

notes.he: הנהנה מקדשי שמים. משום דמפיק קדושה לחולין. כגון דאמר המקדיש הכי] לכשיבואו דמיו יקדשו לא מעל שוב דלא הקדיש בית אלא שכירות הקדיש:
notes.en: [Misuse: one who benefits from items consecrated to Heaven, because he takes sanctity out to non-sacred status. For instance, where the one consecrating said:] When its money comes, let it be consecrated; he no longer misuses, since he did not consecrate the house but consecrated the rent.

messages.text: But how is it possible for the one renting out the house to consecrate money he will receive in the future? After all, a person cannot consecrate an entity that has not yet come into the world.
In accordance with whose opinion is this baraita? It is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Meir, who says: A person can consecrate an entity that has not yet come into the world.

messages.lead: Some say that Rav Pappa said to Abaye, and some say that Rav Mari bar Ḥama said to Rav Ḥisda:

messages.text: Rather, in accordance with who else’s opinion could this baraita be? Certainly it is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Meir.
messages.lead: He said to him (Abaye, or Rav Ḥisda in the second version):

messages.text: On 20b the same exchange names Rami bar Ḥama as the one who asked Rav Ḥisda; here the text reads Rav Mari bar Ḥama.
Mishna
With regard to those obligated to pay valuations, the court repossesses their property to pay their debt to the Temple treasury.

notes.he: [הגזבר] אם ישהום דכיון דלאו לכפרה אתו ולא מהדר ליתנן:
notes.en: Those obligated to pay valuations, one repossesses their property: [the treasurer does,] if they delay them, since they do not come for atonement and he will not take care to give them.

messages.text: With regard to those obligated to bring sin offerings and guilt offerings, the court does not repossess their property; since one is obligated to bring them for atonement he would not delay bringing them.

notes.he: [חייבי חטאות ואשמות אין ממשכנין דכיון דלכפרת עצמו הן זהיר להביאן:
notes.en: [Those obligated to bring sin offerings and guilt offerings, one does not repossess their property: since they are for his own atonement, he is careful to bring them.

messages.text: But with regard to those obligated to bring burnt offerings and peace offerings, the court repossesses their property; since these offerings are not obligatory for atonement, one might delay bringing them.

notes.he: עולות ושלמים. אע"ג דשלמים מכפרת אעשה הואיל ולאו חובה היא עליה לא חשיב לה כפרה ואתי לשהויי הלכך ממשכנין אותן:
notes.en: Mishna. One repossesses their property: [those obligated in] burnt offerings and peace offerings. Even though a peace offering atones for [neglect of] a positive mitzva, since it is not an obligation upon him it is not regarded as atonement, and he may come to delay it; therefore one repossesses their property.

notes.he: חייבי עולה ושלמים ממשכנין אותן דלא אתו לכפרה ויתרשל להביאן]:
notes.en: Those obligated to bring burnt offerings and peace offerings, one repossesses their property: since they do not come for atonement, and he will be negligent in bringing them.]

messages.text: Although one obligated to bring burnt offerings and peace offerings does not achieve atonement until he brings the offering of his own volition, as it is stated: “He shall bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting of his volition” (Leviticus 1:3), nevertheless the court coerces him until he says: I want to do so.

verse.he: אִם־עֹלָה קׇרְבָּנוֹ מִן־הַבָּקָר זָכָר תָּמִים יַקְרִיבֶנּוּ אֶל־פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד יַקְרִיב אֹתוֹ לִרְצֹנוֹ לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה׃
verse.en: If your offering is a burnt offering from the herd, you shall make your offering a male without blemish. You shall bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, for acceptance in your behalf before GOD.

notes.he: האי מתכפר [לו] לא כפרה ממש אלא אע"פ שאין מתקבלין לרצון עד שיתרצה להביאן מעצמו:
notes.en: Even though he does not achieve atonement: this “atonement” is not atonement in the literal sense; rather: even though they are not accepted favorably until he consents to bring them of his own accord.

notes.he: לפני ה' אפילו הכי ממשכנין אותן [וכופין אותו] עד שיאמר רוצה אני:
notes.en: As it is stated: “Of his volition,” before the Lord. Even so, one repossesses their property [and coerces him] until he says: I want to.

messages.text: And likewise, you say the same with regard to women’s bills of divorce. Although one divorces his wife only of his own volition, in any case where the Sages obligated a husband to divorce his wife the court coerces him until he says: I want to do so.

notes.he: אע"ג דגט המעושה פסול כופין אותו עד שיאמר רוצה אני וכשר:
notes.en: And likewise you say with regard to women’s bills of divorce: although a coerced bill of divorce is invalid, one coerces him until he says, “I want to,” and it is valid.

messages.text: Gemara

Sometimes with regard to those obligated to bring sin offerings the court does repossess their property, and likewise there are occasions involving those obligated to bring burnt offerings where the court does not repossess their property.
messages.quote: sin offerings and guilt offerings, the court does not repossess their property

messages.text: With regard to those obligated to bring sin offerings, the court repossesses their property in the case of the sin offering of a nazirite,

If a nazirite shaved after the sacrifice of one of the three nazirite offerings, either the burnt offering, the peace offering, or the sin offering, he has fulfilled his obligation of shaving. And if the blood of one of these offerings was sprinkled on his behalf, the nazirite is permitted to drink wine and to become ritually impure from a corpse.

notes.he: חטאת או עולה או שלמים דג' קרבנות כתובין בו ואמרי' בספרי דבי רב ואחר ישתה הנזיר יין אחר מעשה יחידי:
notes.en: Gemara. Of the three of them: a sin offering, a burnt offering or a peace offering, since three offerings are written for him [the nazirite]. And we say in the Sifrei of the school of Rav: “And afterward the nazirite may drink wine” (Numbers 6:20): after a single act.

messages.text: Therefore, there is a concern that a nazirite who has already sacrificed his burnt offering or peace offering might be negligent with regard to his sin offering and not bring it, and therefore the court repossesses his property in this particular case.

notes.he: [או אעולה או אשלמים או אחטאת יצא] הלכך אם גילח על העולה צריך למשכנו להביא חטאת:
notes.en: Over one of the three of them: [whether over the burnt offering, or the peace offering, or the sin offering, he has fulfilled his obligation]. Therefore, if he shaved over the burnt offering, his property must be repossessed so that he brings the sin offering.

messages.text: With regard to those obligated to bring burnt offerings, the court does not repossess their property in the case of a burnt offering of a woman after childbirth. There is no concern that she might delay bringing her burnt offering, as she is required to bring this offering before partaking of sacrificial food.

notes.he: דלא משתריא בקדשים עד דמתיא לה:
notes.en: The burnt offering of a woman after childbirth: since she is not permitted to eat sacrificial food until she brings it.

notes.he: שאינה יכולה להביא חטאתה עד שתביא עולתה קודם:
notes.en: The burnt offering of a woman after childbirth: who cannot bring her sin offering until she first brings her burnt offering.

messages.text: What is the reason for the ruling that a woman after childbirth is required to bring her burnt offering before she can sacrifice her sin offering? Is it that the verse mentions her burnt offering before it mentions her sin offering, as it is written: “And when the days of her purification are fulfilled…she shall bring a lamb of the first year for a burnt offering, and a young pigeon, or a turtle-dove, for a sin offering” (Leviticus 12:6)?
messages.quote: a burnt offering of a woman after childbirth

verse.he: וּבִמְלֹאת ׀ יְמֵי טׇהֳרָהּ לְבֵן אוֹ לְבַת תָּבִיא כֶּבֶשׂ בֶּן־שְׁנָתוֹ לְעֹלָה וּבֶן־יוֹנָה אוֹ־תֹר לְחַטָּאת אֶל־פֶּתַח אֹהֶל־מוֹעֵד אֶל־הַכֹּהֵן׃
verse.en: On the completion of her period of purification, for either son or daughter, she shall bring to the priest, at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, a lamb in its first year for a burnt offering, and a pigeon or a turtledove for a purgation offering.

notes.he: כלומר מאי טעמא אמרת דעולתה מעכבתה משום דאקדמיה קרא עולה מקמי חטאת דכתיב תביא כבש בן שנתו לעולה וגו':
notes.en: What is it, that the verse placed it first: that is, what is the reason you said that her burnt offering holds her back? Because the verse placed the burnt offering before the sin offering, as it is written: “She shall bring a lamb of the first year for a burnt offering,” and so on.

notes.he: דכתיב אחד לעולה ואחד לחטאת ולא פשעה בה:
notes.en: [Since the verse placed it first: as it is written, “one for a burnt offering and one for a sin offering,” and she will not be negligent with it.

messages.text: The verse mentions her burnt offering before her sin offering only with regard to the reading of the verse, but not with regard to the order of the offerings.

notes.he: שתהא נקראת במקרא תחילה ולא שתקרב תחילה בפרק כל התדיר במסכת זבחים (דף צ.):
notes.en: But doesn’t Rava say: the verse placed it first for its reading: that it be read first in Scripture, and not that it be sacrificed first; in the chapter Kol HaTadir in tractate Zevaḥim (90a).

notes.he: כלומר לקרות העולה קודם לחטאת הקדימה הכתוב אבל להקרבה לא אקדמה:
notes.en: The verse placed it first for its reading: that is, the verse placed the burnt offering before the sin offering for reading it, but not for sacrificing it.

messages.text: If so, there should be a concern that she might first sacrifice her sin offering and delay bringing her burnt offering.
Rather, the court does not repossess the property of those obligated to bring burnt offerings in the case of the burnt offering of a leper,

notes.he: אין צריך למשכן דתניא כו']:
notes.en: Rather, the burnt offering of a leper: there is no need to repossess his property, as it is taught, and so on.]

messages.text: Just as failure to sacrifice his sin offering and his guilt offering prevents the leper from achieving full ritual purity, so too, failure to sacrifice his burnt offering has the same effect and prevents him from achieving full ritual purity.
messages.lead: as it is taught in a baraita that Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yehuda ben Beroka, says:

messages.text: Therefore, the court does not repossess his property, as there is no concern he might delay bringing his burnt offering.

Although one obligated to bring burnt offerings and peace offerings does not achieve atonement until he brings the offering of his own volition, nevertheless, one coerces him until he says: I want to do so.
messages.quote: Although one obligated to bring burnt offerings and peace offerings does not achieve atonement until he brings the offering of his own volition

messages.text: It is written with regard to a burnt offering: “He shall sacrifice it” (Leviticus 1:3), which teaches that one coerces him to bring his burnt offering. One might have thought he brings the offering against his will; therefore, the verse states: “Of his volition” (Leviticus 1:3). How can these texts be reconciled? The court coerces him until he says: I want to do so.

verse.he: אִם־עֹלָה קׇרְבָּנוֹ מִן־הַבָּקָר זָכָר תָּמִים יַקְרִיבֶנּוּ אֶל־פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד יַקְרִיב אֹתוֹ לִרְצֹנוֹ לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה׃
verse.en: If your offering is a burnt offering from the herd, you shall make your offering a male without blemish. You shall bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, for acceptance in your behalf before GOD.

messages.text: A burnt offering requires the consent of the one receiving atonement, as it is stated: “Of his volition.”

notes.he: כלומר המביא עולה צריך להביאה לרצונו:
notes.en: A burnt offering requires consent: that is, one who brings a burnt offering must bring it of his own volition.

messages.text: What is Shmuel teaching us? Didn’t we already learn in the mishna: Although he does not achieve atonement until he brings the offering of his own volition, as it is stated: “He shall bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting of his volition”?
messages.quote: A burnt offering requires the consent

messages.text: No, the statement of Shmuel is necessary with regard to a case where another person separated, i.e., designated, a burnt offering on his behalf.

notes.he: שהיה זה חייב עולה ובא חבירו והפרישה משלו לכפרתו של זה וקאמר שמואל דבעינן שיודיע את המתכפר:
notes.en: Where his fellow separated it for him: this man was obligated to bring a burnt offering, and his fellow came and separated one from his own property for this man’s atonement. And Shmuel says that we require that he inform the one receiving atonement.

notes.he: אם חברו הפריש בגינו עולה שלא צריך להפרישה לרצונו של נודר:
notes.en: Where his fellow separated it for him: if his fellow separated a burnt offering on his behalf, [one might think] it need not be separated with the consent of the one who vowed.

messages.text: Lest you say: When we require the consent of the one receiving atonement, that is only in a case where an animal from his property is separated as his burnt offering, e.g., the court repossesses his property for the sake of his burnt offering. But we do not need his consent if an animal from the property of another is separated as his burnt offering.

notes.he: כגון היכא דב"ד ממשכנין אותו צריך שיאמר רוצה אני:
notes.en: From his own: for example, where the court repossesses his property, he must say: I want to.

notes.he: היכא דמפריש משלו אבל כשמפרישה חבירו בשבילו נימא דניחא ליה שחברו נותנה בשבילו ולא בעינן למישייליה דודאי ניחא ליה:
notes.en: From his own: where he separates it from his own property. But when his fellow separates it for him, we might say he is amenable to his fellow giving it for him, and we need not ask him, since he is certainly amenable.

messages.text: Therefore, Shmuel teaches us that the consent of the one receiving atonement is required even in a case where an animal from the property of another was separated as an offering. The reason is that sometimes he is not amenable to achieving atonement with an item that does not belong to him, and in such a case he will not achieve atonement.

notes.he: דבעינן למישייליה דזמנין דלא ניחא ליה לאיניש כו' הלכך בעינן לדעתו:
notes.en: It teaches us: that we need to ask him, since sometimes a person is not amenable, and so on. Therefore we require his consent.

messages.text: The Gemara raises an objection from a baraita:
With regard to one who says: It is incumbent upon me to bring the sin offering or the guilt offering of so-and-so,

if he does so with the consent of the one obligated to bring the offering he has fulfilled his obligation, but if he does so without the consent of the one obligated to bring the offering he has not fulfilled his obligation.

notes.he: שהודיע את המתכפר:
notes.en: With consent: that he informed the one receiving atonement.

notes.he: אם הקריבה לדעתו של מחוייב יצא המחוייב]:
notes.en: [With consent, he has fulfilled his obligation: if he sacrificed it with the consent of the one obligated, the one obligated has fulfilled his obligation.]

messages.text: With regard to one who says: It is incumbent upon me to bring the burnt offering or the peace offering of so-and-so, whether he does so with the latter’s consent or without his consent, the one obligated to bring the offering has fulfilled his obligation.
This apparently contradicts the statement of Shmuel, who said the bringing of a burnt offering requires the consent of the one obligated to bring the offering.

When that baraita is taught, and states that one fulfills his obligation for his burnt offering without his consent, it is referring to the time of atonement, i.e., the sacrifice. At that stage, his consent is not necessary, as he already consented at the time of separating the animal as an offering.
messages.quote: whether he does so with the latter’s consent or without his consent

notes.he: דלא בעינן דעת בעלים בשעת הקרבה תניא דהא הודיעו בשעת הפרשה ואירצי שנתרצה בדבר:
notes.en: When that is taught: that the owner’s consent is not needed at the time of sacrifice, it is taught because they informed him at the time of separation and he was amenable, i.e., he agreed to the matter.

notes.dh: אמר לך שמואל כי תניא ההיא בשעת כפרה
notes.he: (וברייתא מיירי בשעת הפרשה) וא"ת אמאי פליג אדעולא לוקמא למילתיה דשמואל בשעת כפרה ובריית' מיירי בשעת הפרשה ולא פליג אדעולא וי"ל דסבירא ליה דשמואל מיירי בשעת הפרשה דקאי אמתני' דמשמע דמיירי בשעת הפרשה מדקאמר חייבי עולות אין ממשכנין אותן שזהו בשעת הפרשה:
notes.en: Shmuel could have said to you: when that is taught, it refers to the time of atonement (and the baraita is dealing with the time of separation). And if you say: why does he disagree with Ulla? Let us set Shmuel’s statement at the time of atonement and the baraita at the time of separation, and he would not disagree with Ulla. One can say: the Gemara holds that Shmuel is speaking of the time of separation, as he is commenting on the mishna, which implies it deals with the time of separation, since it says of those obligated to bring burnt offerings that one repossesses their property [the printed Tosafot read “does not repossess”], and that happens at the time of separation.

notes.dh: אמר לך שמואל כי תניא ההיא
notes.he: דעולה בין לדעת ובין שלא לדעת יצא:
notes.en: Shmuel could have said to you: when that is taught: that for a burnt offering, whether with consent or without consent, he has fulfilled his obligation.

notes.he: אינה צריכה דעת הואיל ואירצי בשעת הפרשה שהיה לדעתו ודאי עדיין ניחא ליה באותו (דעת) [עולה]:
notes.en: At the time of atonement: it does not need consent, since he was amenable at the time of separation, which was with his consent; surely he is still amenable to that burnt offering.

messages.text: When I said the consent of the one receiving atonement is required, I was speaking of the time of separating the animal as an offering.

notes.he: דצריך דעת בשעת הפרשה: והא דשמואל דבעי דעת בהפרשה ולא בכפרה:
notes.en: And when I say: that consent is needed at the time of separation. So Shmuel requires consent at separation and not at atonement.

notes.he: [וכי אמינא אנא עולה צריך דעת בשעת הפרשה:
notes.en: [And when I say that a burnt offering requires consent, it is at the time of separation.

messages.text: And Shmuel disagrees with the opinion of Ulla,

notes.he: דאיהו אמר איפכא:
notes.en: Disagrees with Ulla: for he says the reverse.

messages.text: The Sages distinguish between the consent required for a sin offering or a guilt offering and the consent required for a burnt offering or a peace offering only in that a sin offering and a guilt offering require the consent of the one obligated to bring the offering at the time the other person separates the animal for an offering on his behalf, and a burnt offering and a peace offering do not require his consent at the time of separating the animal.

But with regard to both this pair of offerings and that pair of offerings at the time of atonement, the requisite consent is the same for all offerings: If the offering was sacrificed with his consent he has fulfilled his obligation; if it was not sacrificed with his consent he has not fulfilled his obligation.

notes.he: אידי ואידי אחד חטאת ואחד עולה:
notes.en: This and that: both a sin offering and a burnt offering.

messages.text: The Gemara raises an objection to the opinions of both Shmuel and Ulla from a baraita:

One who says: It is incumbent upon me to bring the sin offering or the guilt offering or the burnt offering or the peace offering of so-and-so, if he does this with the consent of the one who is obligated to bring the offering, then that individual has fulfilled his obligation. If he does so without the consent of the one who is obligated to bring the offering, that person has not fulfilled his obligation.

notes.he: אלמא בכולהו בעינן דעת וקשיא לתרוייהו:
notes.en: Without consent he has not fulfilled his obligation: evidently we require consent for all of them, and this is difficult for both of them.

messages.text: This baraita is difficult for the opinion of Shmuel, who holds that one who brings a burnt offering on behalf of another does not require consent at the time of atonement, and it is also difficult according to the opinion of Ulla, who maintains that one who brings a burnt offering on behalf of another does not need consent when the animal is set aside as an offering.

Shmuel establishes the baraita, which requires consent, as referring to the time of separating the animal, and Ulla establishes the baraita as dealing with the required consent at the time of atonement.
messages.quote: without the consent of the one who is obligated to bring the offering, that person has not fulfilled his obligation

notes.he: דלא חלקו ועולא [מוקי לה] בשעת כפרה:
notes.en: Shmuel establishes it at the time of separation: where they did not distinguish; and Ulla [establishes it] at the time of atonement.

messages.text: The baraitot are not difficult, as they do not contradict each other. This one is referring to consent at the time of atonement, and that one is referring to consent at the time of separating the animal.

notes.he: הא דקתני לעיל עולתו ושלמיו של פלוני עלי בין לדעת בין שלא לדעת יצא והך בתרייתא דקתני בכולהו שלא לדעת לא יצא לא קשיין אהדדי חדא בשעת כפרה וחדא בהפרשה לעולא כדאית ליה ולשמואל כדאית ליה:
notes.en: The baraitot are not difficult for each other: what was taught above, “The burnt offering or the peace offering of so-and-so is upon me, whether with consent or without consent, he has fulfilled his obligation,” and this last one, which teaches that for all of them, without consent he has not fulfilled his obligation, are not difficult for each other: one speaks of the time of atonement and one of separation, for Ulla as he holds and for Shmuel as he holds.

notes.he: קמייתא דתני דבין [לדעת ובין] שלא לדעת יצא בשעת הפרשה. אמוראי ודאי פליגי עולא ושמואל]:
notes.en: The baraitot are not difficult for each other: the first, which teaches that whether with consent or without consent he has fulfilled his obligation, refers to the time of separation. The amora’im, Ulla and Shmuel, certainly disagree.]

messages.text: And the baraitot also are not difficult for the opinions of the amora’im. Shmuel establishes the first baraita, which does not require consent for a burnt offering and a peace offering, as referring to the time of atonement, and the last baraita, which requires consent for those offerings, as speaking of the time of separating the animal.

Ulla establishes the baraitot in the reverse manner: The first baraita, which does not require consent for a burnt offering and a peace offering, is dealing with the time of separating the animal, whereas the second baraita is referring to the time of atonement. But the amora’im themselves, Shmuel and Ulla, certainly disagree with each other.

messages.caption: When does an offering brought for someone else need his consent? Shmuel and Ulla, as Rav Pappa reads them

messages.text: Isn’t this summary of the opinions of Shmuel and Ulla obvious?

Rav Pappa’s summary is necessary, lest you say: What is the meaning of that which Shmuel says, that the consent of the one obligated to bring the offering is required at the time of separating the animal? Shmuel means that consent is required not only at the stage of atonement but even at the time of separating the animal.

notes.he: דבין בהפרשה בין בכפרה בעי דעת. ואע"ג דהויא הך קמייתא תיובתיה דקתני דעולה לא בעיא דעת דהאי שינויא דשני הש"ס לעיל אמר לך שמואל כי תניא ההיא בשעת כפרה כו' לאו מילתא היא קמ"ל רב פפא דקאמר לאמוראי נמי לא קשיין שמואל מוקי קמייתא בשעת כפרה מכלל דשמואל בכפרה לא בעי דעת ושינויא דשנין לעיל שינויא הוא:
notes.en: Even at the time of separation: that he requires consent both at separation and at atonement. And even though this first baraita, which teaches that a burnt offering does not require consent, is a refutation of him, because the answer the Gemara gave above, “Shmuel could have said to you: when that is taught it refers to the time of atonement,” is no real answer. Rav Pappa teaches us, by saying that the baraitot are also not difficult for the amora’im, that Shmuel establishes the first baraita at the time of atonement; by implication, Shmuel does not require consent at atonement, and the answer given above is a real answer.

notes.dh: מאי בשעת הפרשה דקאמר שמואל אף בשעת הפרשה
notes.he: וא"ת מ"מ הא פליג דלשמואל צריכה דעת אף בשעת הפרשה וכ"ש בשעת כפרה ולעולא צריכה בשעת כפרה דווקא ולא בשעת הפרשה וי"ל דמ"מ דבכה"ג דפליגי השתא לא הוו פליגי ונראה לר"י טעמא דשמואל ועולא דהא דאמר שמואל עולה ושלמים צריכין דעת בשעת הפרשה משום דלא ניחא ליה לאיניש להתכפר במילתא דלא דידיה אבל בשעת כפרה אינו צריך דמשום סמיכה אין צריך לדעתו כיון דאינם באים לכפר על חטאו אבל חטאת ואשם שהם באים על חטא וצריכין להתוודות [בשעת] סמיכה בעינן [דעת] בשעת כפרה ועולא סבירא ליה דאפילו בעולה ושלמים רוצה לקיים מצות סמיכה הלכך בעינן דעתו בשעת כפרה אבל בשעת הפרשה לא בעינן דעת אלא בחטאת משום דלא ניחא ליה לאינש לכפרה במילתא דלאו דידיה אבל עולה ושלמים דלא לכפרה קאתי כולי האי אינו צריך דעת בשעת הפרשה:
notes.en: What is “at the time of separation” that Shmuel said? Even at the time of separation: and if you say: they disagree in any case, for according to Shmuel it requires consent even at the time of separation, and all the more so at the time of atonement, while according to Ulla it requires consent only at the time of atonement and not at the time of separation? One can say: in any case, they would not disagree in the way they disagree now. And the Ri thinks the reasoning of Shmuel and Ulla is this. Shmuel says burnt offerings and peace offerings require consent at the time of separation because a person is not amenable to achieving atonement with something that is not his; but at the time of atonement they do not need it, since for the sake of the laying of hands his consent is not needed, as they do not come to atone for his sin. But a sin offering and a guilt offering, which come for a sin and require confession at the laying of hands, require consent at the time of atonement. And Ulla holds that even with burnt offerings and peace offerings a person wants to fulfill the mitzva of laying of hands, so we require his consent at the time of atonement; but at the time of separation consent is required only for a sin offering, because a person is not amenable to atonement with something that is not his, whereas burnt offerings and peace offerings, which do not come for atonement to that degree, need no consent at the time of separation.

notes.he: אף בשעת הפרשה כלומר דבשעת כפרה נמי והיינו דעולא:
notes.en: Even at the time of separation: that is, at the time of atonement as well, and that is Ulla’s view.

messages.text: And even though according to this interpretation the first baraita, which says that consent is not required for a burnt offering and for a peace offering, would be a refutation of the opinion of Shmuel, that difficulty would not deter him from holding such an opinion.

notes.he: ואע"ג דהויא הך קמייתא תיובתיה הא דאמרה דבין לדעת ובין שלא לדעת יצא דאוקימנא בשעת כפרה:
notes.en: And even though this first baraita is a refutation of him: where it said that whether with consent or without consent he has fulfilled his obligation, which we established as referring to the time of atonement.

messages.text: Therefore, Rav Pappa teaches us that the baraitot do not contradict the opinions of Shmuel and Ulla, which indicates that Shmuel holds that consent is required only when the animal is separated, but not at the time of atonement.

notes.he: דבשעת הפרשה גרידא קאמר. [וודאי] פליגי:
notes.en: It teaches us: that he spoke of the time of separation alone. [And certainly] they disagree.

messages.text: And likewise, you say the same with regard to women’s bills of divorce. Although one can divorce his wife only of his own volition, in any case where the Sages obligated a husband to divorce his wife, the court coerces him until he says: I want to do so.
messages.quote: And likewise, you say the same with regard to women’s bills of divorce

messages.text: Concerning one who delivered a declaration preemptively invalidating a bill of divorce by announcing before giving the bill of divorce that he is not doing so of his own free will, his declaration is a valid declaration that cancels the bill of divorce.

notes.dh: האי מאן דמסר מודעא אגיטא מודעיה מודעא
notes.he: (פסק) לפיכך נהגו העולם לבטל כל מודעי ומודעי דאתו מגו מודעי בשעת כתיבת הגט ובשעת הנתינה דחיישינן שמא בטל אותו:
notes.en: One who delivered a declaration about a bill of divorce, his declaration is a declaration: (a ruling). Therefore people are accustomed to cancel every declaration, and declarations within declarations, at the time the bill of divorce is written and at the time it is given, since we are concerned lest [an earlier declaration] invalidate it.

notes.he: שהיו אונסין אותו לתת גט ואמר לעדים הוו עדים שאנוס אני:
notes.en: One who delivered a declaration about a bill of divorce: they were forcing him to give a bill of divorce, and he said to witnesses: Be witnesses that I am being forced.

notes.he: ולא הוי גיטא:
notes.en: His declaration is a declaration: and it is not a bill of divorce.

messages.text: Isn’t that obvious?
messages.quote: his declaration is a valid declaration

messages.text: No, the statement of Rav Sheshet is necessary in a case where they coerced him to give a bill of divorce and he declared that he was not giving it of his own free will, but later he agreed to give the bill of divorce of his own volition without explicitly retracting his original declaration that he was coerced.

notes.he: אחרי כן:
notes.en: That they coerced him: afterward.

notes.he: לתת הגט והמודעא לא ביטל:
notes.en: And he agreed: to give the bill of divorce, and did not cancel the declaration.

notes.he: לא צריכא דעשויה אחרי המודעה ואירצי ושתק ונתן בשתיקה:
notes.en: It is necessary only where they coerced him after the declaration, and he agreed, kept silent, and gave it in silence.

messages.text: Lest you say: Merely by giving the bill of divorce he has canceled his earlier declaration that he was coerced, Rav Sheshet therefore teaches us that his original declaration that he was coerced is still in effect and the bill of divorce is canceled.

notes.he: מסתמא בטלה למודעא קמ"ל רב ששת דלא וממתניתין יליף טעמא דא"כ ליתני כופין אותו עד שיתן:
notes.en: Lest you say: presumably he canceled the declaration. Rav Sheshet teaches us that he did not. And he derives the reason from the mishna: for if so, let it teach: one coerces him until he gives it.

notes.he: מדנתן בטולי בטליה למודעיה:
notes.en: Lest you say: since he gave it, he canceled his declaration.

notes.he: דלא:
notes.en: It teaches us: that he did not.

messages.text: The reason is that if it were so, i.e., if his original declaration is canceled even without an explicit retraction, let the mishna teach: The court coerces him until he gives the bill of divorce of his own volition. What is the significance of the clause: The court coerces him until he says: I want to do so? This indicates that the court coerces him until he explicitly cancels his original declaration.

notes.he: דבהכי סגיא בנתינת סתם ליתני כופין אותו עד שיתן מאי עד שיאמר קמ"ל דבטיל למודעיה ויאמר רוצה אני:
notes.en: For if so: that giving it without comment is enough, let it teach: one coerces him until he gives it. What is “until he says”? It teaches us that he must cancel his declaration and say: I want to.

notes.he: הדרן עלך האומר משקלי:
notes.en: We will return to you, HaOmer Mishkali.

messages.text: הדרן עלך האומר משקלי · Hadran alakh HaOmer Mishkali: we will return to you, chapter 5, “One Who Says: My Weight [Is Incumbent upon Me].”
Chapter 6 · שום היתומים · Shum HaYetomim: appraising orphans’ property, and collecting a valuation by seizing the debtor’s property.
Mishna

One proclaims, i.e., publicly announces, the appraisal of the property inherited by minor orphans, which is being sold to repay their father’s debt, for thirty days, in order to receive the maximal price.

notes.he: ב"ד היורדים לנכסי יתומים למוכרן להגבות לבעל חוב שמין את הקרקע ומכריזין ל' יום כל הרוצה ליקח יבא ויקח:
notes.en: Mishna. The appraisal of orphans: a court that goes down to the property of orphans to sell it in order to collect for a creditor appraises the land and proclaims for thirty days: whoever wishes to buy, let him come and buy.

notes.he: וא"ת אמאי נקט יתומים אפי' כ"ע נמי אם באו בית דין לירד בנכסיהן כדי לפרוע לאשה כתובתה או חובו לב"ח צריך שומת ב"ד ל' יום כדאיתא בפ' המפקיד (ב"מ לה:) מאימת אכיל פירי מכי שלמי יומי אכרזתא אלמא לכל אדם שבא לירד לנכסיהן צריכי שומת ב"ד א"כ אמאי נקט יתומים וי"ל דתנא יתומים לרבותא דמהו דתימא דליהוי יתומים כהקדש ולבעי שומת בית דין ס' יום קמ"ל דשוין לכל אדם:
notes.en: Mishna. The appraisal of orphans, thirty days: and if you say: why does it mention orphans? Even with anyone, if the court came to go down to their property to pay a wife her marriage contract or a creditor his debt, a court appraisal of thirty days is needed, as stated in chapter HaMafkid (Bava Metzia 35b): from when may he eat the produce? From when the days of proclamation are completed. Evidently anyone whose property is gone down to requires a court appraisal. If so, why mention orphans? One can say: the tanna taught orphans as a novelty: lest you say orphans should be like consecrated property and require a court appraisal of sixty days, it teaches us that they are like everyone else.

notes.he: כשנצרכין ב"ד למכור מנכסי יתומים או לפרנסה או (לכסות) [לכתובה] או לשום דבר צריך לשומן ולהכריז (כל) שלשים יום [בבקר ובערב] כדמפרש בגמרא אומר שדה פלונית בסימניה ובמצריה כך היא יפה וכך היא שומא כדי שישמעו בנ"א ויבואו ליקח ויוסיף כל אחד על חברו ליתן:
notes.en: The appraisal of orphans, thirty days: when the court needs to sell from the property of orphans, whether for their sustenance or for a marriage contract or for anything else, it must appraise it and proclaim for thirty days [in the morning and in the evening], as the Gemara explains: one says, the field of so-and-so, by its markers and by its borders, such is its quality and such is its appraisal; so that people will hear and come to buy, and each will add to his fellow’s offer.

messages.text: And one proclaims the appraisal of consecrated property that is being sold by the Temple treasury for sixty days, and one proclaims it in the morning and in the evening.

notes.he: גזבר המוכר קרקע של הקדש:
notes.en: And the appraisal of consecrated property: a treasurer who sells land belonging to the Temple.

notes.he: כשרוצין לפדות שדה הקדש:
notes.en: And the appraisal of consecrated property [sixty days]: when they wish to redeem a consecrated field.

messages.text: Gemara
What is different about those times that one proclaims the appraisal of the property specifically in the morning and in the evening?
messages.quote: in the morning and in the evening

messages.text: One proclaims during the time that workers leave to work in the fields and during the time that workers enter the city after completing their workday.

notes.dh: בשעת הוצאת פועלים ובשעת הכנסת פועלים
notes.he: פירוש בשעת הוצאת פועלים ממלאכתן ובשעת הכנסתן למלאכה ואין זו סדר המשנה דנקט בבקר ובערב ורב יהודה מפרש ערב תחילה ואחר כך בקר וי"ל משום דכן הסדר לפי שאינו רוצה לבטל ממלאכתו לפיכך אין דרך למימר להו סיירוה ניהלי דאם לא כן למה להמתין עד הערב ונשאליה להו מה ראו הא כל היום יש לו רשות לשיוליה לפיכך הוצרכו לרב יהודה לפרש כן שבשעת יציאה ממלאכתן אמר להו סיירוה ניהלי שאז אין מבטלין ממלאכתם ולמחרת כשנזכר מה דאמר להו לאורתא אזיל לשאול ומש"ה אין לפרש איפכא בשעת הוצאת הפועלים מביתם ונכנסין במלאכתן ובשעת הכנסתן בביתם ויוצאין ממלאכתן לפי דאין דרך לעשות כן כדפירשנו ועוד דאין ליישב לשון הספר על זה ובתוספות הארכתי הרבה בזה והביאו ההיא דריש השוכר את הפועלים (ב"מ פג. ושם:) רב אסי אמר פועל בכניסתו משלו וביציאתו משל בעל הבית:
notes.en: At the time the workers go out and at the time the workers come in: meaning, at the time the workers go out from their work, and at the time they come in to their work. [So Tosafot read it, the reverse of the Davidson English; Rabbeinu Gershom reads it the same way.] And this is not the order of the mishna, which said “in the morning and in the evening,” while Rav Yehuda explains the evening first and then the morning. One can say: that is the right order, because he does not want to take them from their work, so it is not usual to say “Examine it for me” to them [while they work]. For otherwise, why wait until the evening to ask them what they saw? He is free to ask them all day. Therefore Rav Yehuda needed to explain it so: when they leave their work, he says to them, “Examine it for me,” since then he does not take them from their work; and the next day, when he remembers what he told them the evening before, he goes to ask. And therefore one should not explain the reverse, at the time the workers go out of their homes and enter their work and at the time they come into their homes and leave their work, because that is not the usual way, as we explained; and furthermore, the wording of the text cannot be reconciled with that. In the Tosafot I wrote at great length on this, and they cited the passage at the beginning of HaSokher et HaPoalim (Bava Metzia 83a–b): Rav Asi said: a worker’s coming in is on his own time, and his going out is on the employer’s.

messages.text: One proclaims during the time that workers leave to work in the fields, so that if there is a person who is amenable to purchasing the property, he may say to the workers: Go and examine the property for me.

notes.he: ראו אם יפה היא:
notes.en: Examine it for me: see whether it is good.

notes.he: לערב כשיוצאין הפועלין ממלאכתן מכריזין כדי שישמע בעה"ב ואומר להו [לפועלין] זילו סיירוה ניהלי:
notes.en: At the time the workers go out: in the evening, when the workers leave their work, one proclaims, so that the householder will hear and say to [the workers]: Go, examine it for me.

messages.text: And one proclaims during the time that workers enter the city so that that individual will be reminded that he said to the workers that they should inspect the property, and he will go and ask them for their opinion of it.

notes.he: בעל הבית באורתא מאי דאמר לפועלים בצפרא:
notes.en: That he will be reminded: the householder, in the evening, of what he said to the workers in the morning.

notes.he: אם יפה היא:
notes.en: And ask them: whether it is good.

notes.he: בבקר נמי מכריזין כי היכי דמדכר בעה"ב מה שאמר לפועלים אמש (ליזיל) דלישיילינהו אם ראוה כמה היא יפה:
notes.en: And at the time the workers come in: one also proclaims in the morning, so that the householder will remember what he said to the workers the night before, and ask them whether they saw it and how good it is.

messages.text: That explanation is also taught in a baraita:

One proclaims the appraisal of the property inherited by minor orphans for thirty days, and one proclaims the appraisal of consecrated property for sixty days. And one proclaims it in the morning and in the evening, during the time that workers leave to work in the fields and during the time that workers enter the city after completing their workday.

The field of so-and-so that is identifiable by its markers and by its borders, such is its quality, i.e., it produces such-and-such quantities of grain annually, and such is its appraisal; anyone who wishes to purchase the field let him come and purchase it.

notes.he: כך וכך היא עושה תבואה:
notes.en: Such is its quality: it produces such-and-such an amount of grain.

notes.he: בכך וכך שמאוה ב"ד:
notes.en: Such is its appraisal: at such-and-such the court appraised it.

notes.he: להוצאת תבואה ופירות כך וכך היא שומא בכך וכך דמים ואם המלוה רוצה לעכב בכך ששמו ב"ד אין צריך להכריז אלא אוקימנא ליה ביד המלוה מיד:
notes.en: Such is its quality: for producing grain and fruit; such is its appraisal: at such-and-such a sum. And if the lender wants to keep it at what the court appraised, there is no need to proclaim; rather, we place it in the lender’s hand at once.

notes.dh: [שדה פלונית כך היא יפה וכך כורין היא עושה וכך היא שומא
notes.he: כלומר בכך וכך ממון שמוה ב"ד]:
notes.en: [The field of so-and-so, such is its quality, so many kor it produces, and such is its appraisal: that is, at such-and-such a sum the court appraised it.]

messages.text: The field is being sold in order to give the proceeds to a wife as payment of her marriage contract, or in order to give a creditor payment of a deceased man’s debt.

notes.he: שיפרע לאשה או לבעל חוב:
notes.en: And let him buy on condition: that he pay the wife or the creditor.

messages.text: Why do I need the one making the proclamation to say that the field is being sold in order to give the proceeds to a wife as payment of her marriage contract or in order to give a creditor payment of his debt?
messages.quote: anyone who wishes to purchase the field let him come and purchase it

notes.he: לאכרוזי על מנת ליתן כו':
notes.en: Why do I need: to proclaim “in order to give,” and so on.

messages.text: This declaration is necessary as there are individuals for whom it is preferable to do business with a creditor, as he is lenient with dinars and will accept even damaged coins, and there are others for whom it is preferable to deal with a wife, as she takes her money bit by bit, i.e., in incremental payments.

notes.he: פורתא פורתא ואיכא לוקח דניחא ליה לפרוע לבעל חוב דמיקל בזוזי שנוטל זוזים שבורים וחסרים שאין דרך סוחרים מקפידין בכך:
notes.en: Bit by bit: little by little. And there is a buyer who prefers to pay a creditor, who is lenient with dinars, accepting broken and deficient coins, since merchants do not usually mind that.

notes.he: לקנות כדי למיהב [דמיה] לבעל חוב דמיקל בזוזי שמי שפורע [לב"ח] אין מניחין לו כל כך לבדוק אזוזי דאמרי ליה ממארי רשותיך פארי איפרע:
notes.en: For there are those who prefer: to buy in order to give [its price] to a creditor, who is lenient with dinars; for one who pays [a creditor] is not given much chance to check the dinars, as people say to him: “From your bad debtor, take even bran in payment.”

notes.he: ואיכא דניחא ליה ללוקח למיהב דמיה לאשה משום דשקלה על יד על יד כשהיא צריכה להוציא ולא בבת אחת:
notes.en: And there are buyers who prefer to give the price to a wife, because she takes it bit by bit, whenever she needs to spend, and not all at once.

messages.text: Continued on 22a: how long is the proclamation? Rabbi Meir says thirty days for orphans and sixty for consecrated property, Rabbi Yehuda sixty and ninety, and the Rabbis sixty for both.
